entry.title: Earhart Expedition: Investigating the Taraia Object

media:group.media:title: Earhart Expedition: Investigating the Taraia Object
media:group.media:description:
The science is underway on Nikumaroro. The Taraia Object expedition team is putting a long-standing Amelia Earhart hypothesis to the test, using research and technology to investigate an object identified in satellite imagery.
Beyond the search for answers about Amelia Earhart and Fred Noonan’s disappearance, the expedition and its partnership with Kiribati are generating valuable new data about the remote South Pacific island of Nikumaroro.
Nikumaroro is part of the Phoenix Islands Protected Area and has been designated as an Important Bird Area by BirdLife International.
Whatever the investigation reveals, the team is building knowledge that will contribute to a better understanding of this remote island and one of aviation history’s enduring mysteries.
Read the latest update: https://www.purdue.edu/newsroom/2026/Q4/earhart-expedition-update-underwater-survey-of-taraia-object-begins/

entry.title: Earhart Expedition: The Team Arrives at Nikumaroro

media:group.media:title: Earhart Expedition: The Team Arrives at Nikumaroro
media:group.media:description:
The Taraia Object expedition team has arrived at Nikumaroro! After days at sea, the team has reached the remote South Pacific island where it will begin the next phase of its search for answers about Amelia Earhart’s disappearance.
Excitement is building as the team prepares to make landfall, bringing the expedition one step closer to its mission to investigate the mystery surrounding the pioneering aviator’s disappearance.
Follow along in the search for Amelia Earhart’s lost aircraft and stay tuned for more updates from the expedition.
Get the latest update: https://www.purdue.edu/newsroom/2026/Q4/earhart-expedition-update-crew-arrives-at-nikumaroro-launches-critical-phase-of-amelia-earhart-plane-search/

entry.title: Earhart Expedition: The People Behind the Mission

media:group.media:title: Earhart Expedition: The People Behind the Mission
media:group.media:description:
The heart of the Taraia Object expedition is a 17-member-strong team of scientists, divers, filmmakers and researchers. Meet a few of them and discover why they are “proud to be the people who could solve an enduring mystery once and for all.”
🧭 Rick Pettigrew, Archaeological Legacy Institute (ALI), project director
As the architect of this historic investigation, Pettigrew has high hopes for the team. “I don’t see anything stopping us,” he said. “We have experienced people who know their specialties and are confident in their abilities.”
🦀 Ren LaRocca, ALI, assistant
LaRocca brings firsthand experience in navigating Nikumaroro, an island that is bigger and more dynamic than people think. “Going to Nikumaroro in 2017 was a special moment,” he said. There are “no mosquitoes, snakes or spiders,” but you do have to watch out for the coconut crabs.
🚂 Steve Schultz, Purdue senior vice president and general counsel, field assistant
Schultz is leading the team of Purdue specialists on this mission. “We’re all geared up for adventure,” he said. “The overwhelming sentiment right now is excitement and also a singular focus on getting the equipment organized and testing it.”
Learn more at amelia.prf.org.

entry.title: Earhart Expedition: Final leg of travel, next step in investigating a mystery

media:group.media:title: Earhart Expedition: Final leg of travel, next step in investigating a mystery
media:group.media:description:
In their first few hours at sea, the Taraia Object expedition team encountered rain and rough seas and enjoyed a hot meal of chicken stew.
“(The ship) doesn’t have all the creature comforts we’re accustomed to, but the Marin Mainiku has everything we need,” said Steve Schultz, the university’s senior vice president and general counsel who serves as the Purdue team lead for the expedition. “This isn’t a pleasure cruise. But it’s our home for the next three weeks, and we’re happy to be aboard and underway.”
The team of 17 scientists and specialists is bound for Nikumaroro in the South Pacific. Upon arrival, they will navigate the rugged interior of the island to reach the lagoon they believe contains Amelia Earhart’s missing plane.
Get the latest update: https://www.purdue.edu/newsroom/2026/Q4/earhart-expedition-update-crew-begins-6-day-sea-voyage-to-south-pacific-atoll-nikumaroro/

entry.title: Taraia Object team’s next stop: Nikumaroro ️

media:group.media:title: Taraia Object team’s next stop: Nikumaroro ️
media:group.media:description: After three days and thousands of miles, the Archaeological Legacy Institute, Purdue Research Foundation and Purdue University expedition team have arrived in Tarawa, Kiribati, where they are making final preparations before a six-day ocean voyage to Nikumaroro, a remote island in the South Pacific. Once there, they will investigate the Taraia Object to determine if it is Amelia Earhart’s missing plane.
